capabilities.detail: Attached and detached while Windows runs, from Configuration > USB Devices, with QMP device_add usb-host and never in the boot plan, so a device that cannot be claimed never stops Windows from starting. Devices without a macOS driver attach as the logged-in user. Devices macOS has a driver for (keyboards, mice, disks, most audio devices) need the com.apple.vm.device-access entitlement or root before libusb will take them from macOS; Veil checks QEMU's attached property after each attach and removes a device that was not claimed. Devices return to the Mac before Windows stops or suspends.
capabilities.title: USB device passthrough
Bridged networking
capabilities.prerequisite: macOS exposes bridged networking through the vmnet framework, which requires root or the com.apple.vm.networking entitlement that Apple grants case by case.
capabilities.alternative: Usermode NAT already gives the guest outbound network access. Reaching the guest from this Mac works through a loopback port forward, which is how the guest agent and the shared folder are reached.
capabilities.detail: Not added to the boot plan: QEMU exits when it cannot open the vmnet interface, so offering this would trade a working network for a VM that does not boot.

capabilities.title: Host-only networking
capabilities.prerequisite: Also a vmnet mode, so it carries the same root or entitlement requirement as bridged networking.
capabilities.alternative: Loopback port forwards give this Mac private access to guest services without exposing them to any network, which is the isolation host-only mode is usually wanted for.
capabilities.detail: Not added to the boot plan, for the same reason as bridged networking.

capabilities.title: Usermode NAT networking
capabilities.detail: The shipping default. The guest reaches the internet, and this Mac reaches guest services through loopback-scoped port forwards. Nothing on the local network can reach the guest, which is the intended isolation.

privilegedHelperDecision: Parallels ships a signed system extension and a privileged helper; Veil runs QEMU as the logged-in user, which is why it needs no admin password. The bridged and host-only network modes require root on macOS, as does taking a USB device away from a macOS driver, so closing them means adopting a privileged helper installed with SMAppService, or the Apple-granted vm.networking and vm.device-access entitlements. Running QEMU under sudo is refused: it would put a user-controlled command line and a network-reachable guest behind root. The decision is open and deliberately not made by this report.
nextActions: The bridged and host-only network modes need a root-privileged helper that Veil does not ship. This is an open product decision, not pending implementation work.
Do not work around it by running QEMU under sudo. That puts a user-controlled command line and a network-reachable guest behind root.
